responsibility: This module is GCC’s target backend for the TI PRU processor family, covering the machine-specific configuration, instruction selection, ABI handling, and target diagnostics needed to turn GCC IR into PRU assembly. Its core is the main backend implementation and machine description, where pru.cc/pru.c and pru.md define target hooks, frame layout, calling conventions, prologue/epilogue expansion, builtin lowering, low-overhead loop and reorg support, operand/address legality, and the RTL patterns for PRU instructions; accompanying predicates, constraints, and ALU zero-extension fragments supply the recognizer vocabulary and operand semantics used by those patterns. The module also defines static target properties and toolchain conventions in pru.h, command-line target options and ABI selection in pru.opt and pru-opts.h, front-end integration for PRU-specific pragmas and address spaces such as CTABLE_ENTRY and __regio_symbol in pru-pragma, and PRU-only pass scheduling and checks in pru-passes to diagnose unsupported TI ABI or minimal-runtime constructs early. Together these files distinguish the module as the complete PRU code-generation port, including constant-table and I/O-register support specific to PRU hardware, rather than generic optimization or front-end logic.
